verdicts.rewritten_summary: Washington Blade (2025-04-10): Argentine trans activists told the Blade the community faces a 'chaotic, desperate' situation under President Milei, who eliminated the national Women/Gender/Diversity Ministry and dismissed trans hires made under the federal Trans Labor Quota Law (1% of public-sector posts), which activists say is no longer being implemented. Milei's Feb 5 2025 decree restricts minors' access to gender-affirming surgeries and hormone treatments. The 2012 Gender Identity Law (legal gender change without medical intervention, 'X' DNI marker since 2021) remains formally in force but is no longer guaranteed, activists report.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Agencia Presentes (2026-03-19), national hate-crime observatory: at least 227 hate crimes against LGBT+ people in Argentina in 2025 — up 62% year-on-year, one every 38 hours, the worst of the observatory's ten years. Trans women and travestis were 62.5% of victims (142 of 227); 64.8% of cases (147) were physical violence against bodily integrity; perpetrators were predominantly security-force personnel and unidentified attackers in public space, with beatings the main modality; the surge is attributed to the government's 'cultural battle' and hate discourse. The same period saw DNU 62/2025 restricting minors' gender-affirming treatments.
verdicts.note: national framework claimed by record text; no region-specific source covers it (rule 1/5 keep)

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Agencia Presentes (2025-02-06): Milei's government published DNU 62/2025 amending Article 11 of the 2012 Gender Identity Law to bar under-18s from gender-affirming surgical and hormonal interventions, and DNU 61/2025 altering prison-sentencing law to change placement of trans detainees. Legal experts and LGBT+ organisations call both decrees unconstitutional and say abruptly suspending adolescent treatments endangers trans youth; the decrees face judicial challenge. They apply nationally, to every province.
